# artcoded

The artcoded backoffice in your terminal: invoices, expenses, timesheets, dossiers, documents, templates…
A single binary (Go, no dependency) for Linux x86_64 and arm64, and a docker image.

```sh
artcoded dashboard              # the most useful figures: tables and charts
artcoded expenses list --help   # the manual of an action: options and examples
artcoded expenses add ~/Downloads/receipt.pdf
artcoded invoices download  # no id: choose the invoice in a list
artcoded timesheets log 8   # 8 hours today
```

## Install

<!-- install:start (generated by the release workflow, see scripts/readme-install.sh) -->
Latest release: **v2027.0.6** · [all releases](https://github.com/openartcoded/artcoded-cli/releases)

Install or update (Linux, x86_64 or arm64):

```sh
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openartcoded/artcoded-cli/main/install.sh | sh
```

The latest build of `main`: `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openartcoded/artcoded-cli/main/install.sh | sh -s -- edge` · a given version: `... | sh -s -- v2027.0.6`

Docker (linux amd64 / arm64): `docker pull nbittich/artcoded-cli`, see [Docker](#docker).
<!-- install:end -->

The script puts `artcoded` in `/usr/local/bin` (or `~/.local/bin`), or where it already is: running it
again updates it. `ARTCODED_INSTALL_DIR` chooses another place. Binaries are built for Linux, x86_64 (amd64)
and arm64, with a `checksums.txt` the script checks. Elsewhere: `go install github.com/openartcoded/artcoded-cli@latest`
(the binary is then called `artcoded-cli`), or the docker image.

### Updates

Once a day, in a terminal, `artcoded` checks the latest release and asks before installing it (same
install script, same place). `artcoded update` installs it now. `DISABLE_AUTO_UPDATE=true` turns the
check off; it never runs in scripts, in docker, or for a dev / `edge` build.

### Docker

`nbittich/artcoded-cli` (linux amd64 / arm64): `:latest` and `:<version>` for the releases, `:edge` for
`main`. The configuration and the tokens are in the `/data` volume.

```sh
docker volume create artcoded
# setup, once (asked in the terminal; or ARTCODED_* variables, see Configuration)
docker run --rm -it -v artcoded:/data nbittich/artcoded-cli init
docker run --rm -it -v artcoded:/data nbittich/artcoded-cli dashboard
```

From the sources (Go 1.26+):

```sh
make build          # ./artcoded
make install        # into $GOBIN (~/go/bin)
make dist           # every platform in dist/, with checksums.txt
```

Shell completion: `source <(artcoded completion bash)` (or `zsh`).

## First run

The first run asks the configuration and logs in; it is saved **only when the login works**, to
`~/.config/artcoded-cli.yml` (permissions 600). Run `artcoded init` to change it.

```
Backoffice url (to read its keycloak settings, optional): https://backoffice.example.org
✓ found the keycloak settings of the backoffice
Backend url [https://api.example.org]:
Keycloak url [https://auth.example.org]:
Keycloak realm [Artcoded]:
Keycloak client id [artcoded]:
Login method: 1) password  2) browser  3) device
Username: …
Password: …
✓ logged in as nordine (ADMIN), configuration saved to ~/.config/artcoded-cli.yml
```

To start over: `artcoded reset` logs out, forgets the configuration and the tokens, then offers the setup.

Giving the backoffice url fills the rest from its runtime config (`/assets/config/config.json`).
Tokens are cached (`~/.cache/artcoded/`) and refreshed; the password is only used when the
session expired.

Without a terminal: `artcoded init --backend-url … --keycloak-url … --realm … --client-id … --username … --password …`.

### Login methods

| method     | how                                                  | keycloak needs                                      |
|------------|------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------|
| `password` | username + password of the config (default)          | *Direct access grants* on the client                |
| `browser`  | opens the keycloak login page, comes back on `127.0.0.1` | *Standard flow* + redirect uri `http://127.0.0.1:53682/*` |
| `device`   | shows a code to confirm in any browser (ssh, servers) | *OAuth 2.0 Device Authorization Grant*              |

With 2FA (OTP) on the account, use `browser` or `device`.

### Self-signed certificates (local setup)

When the backend or keycloak certificate is not trusted, the setup asks how to trust it:
the pem file of your certificate authority (`ca_file`, e.g. mkcert's `rootCA.pem`), or no check at all
(`insecure: true`, local development only). Later: `artcoded config set ca_file ~/ca.pem`.
Instead of a plain text password: `password_command: "pass show artcoded"`.

## Keycloak: one client to add

The backoffice client (`frontend-client`) only allows the browser flow with the backoffice urls.
Add a client for the cli (the backend accepts it as is: it checks the realm roles, not the client):

1. *Clients → Create client*: client type **OpenID Connect**, client id **`artcoded`**.
2. *Capability config*: **Client authentication: off** (public client), then check
   - **Standard flow** (login method `browser`)
   - **Direct access grants** (login method `password`)
   - **OAuth 2.0 Device Authorization Grant** (login method `device`)

   Only the ones you use are needed.
3. *Login settings*: **Valid redirect URIs**: `http://127.0.0.1:53682/*` (browser login; another port: set
   `redirect_port` in the config). Web origins: none.
4. Nothing else: the realm roles (`ADMIN`, `REGULATOR_OR_ACCOUNTANT`) are in the token by default
   (*roles* client scope).

The errors of keycloak come with a hint (e.g. *enable 'Direct access grants' on the client*).

## Usage

```
artcoded <module> <action> [arguments] [--flags]
artcoded <module> --help            the actions of a module
artcoded <module> <action> --help   manual of an action (NAME, OPTIONS, EXAMPLES), paged
artcoded menu [<module>]            interactive menu, only when asked
```

A flag an action does not know (a typo like `--archive`) is reported.

- `--online` on a list / show action opens that page of the backoffice in the browser instead
  (`artcoded invoices list --archived --online`; needs `frontend_url` in the config).
- `--demo` masks the amounts and the names of clients and people (screen sharing); `demo: "true"` in the
  config makes it the default. The demo mode of the backoffice masks the dashboard too.
- `artcoded --version` (or `-V`) prints the version.

The module list (`artcoded`, `artcoded help`) shows only what the menu of the backoffice shows you: a
module hidden in the settings (e.g. the gallery) is not listed. It is the menu last read from the backend
(`artcoded menu`, the dashboard and every command reading the menu refresh it).

Lists show one set at a time, like the backoffice: `expenses list` shows the expenses **to process**
(in no dossier yet), `--processed` the ones already in a dossier; `invoices list --archived`,
`dossiers list --closed` likewise.

**Missing arguments are asked** in a terminal: ids are chosen in a list (type text to filter), files
are asked one path per line (drag & drop works), long texts open `$EDITOR`. Without a terminal (scripts,
cron) a missing argument is an error naming the flag.

Common flags: `--json` (raw json), `--yes`/`-y` (no questions, confirms), `--out <file|dir>`,
`--open` (open what is downloaded), `--stdout`, `--page n --size n`, `--verbose`.

The interactive menu (`artcoded menu`) shows the entries of *Settings → Menu* of the backoffice that are visible for you,
in the same order (`admin menu-toggle` changes them): a link hidden in the settings hides its modules.
Statistics come with Home, the toolbox with Administration (a tab of that page in the backoffice), and
Templates is added for an admin while the backend menu has no link for it (like the backoffice does).

| module | what |
|---|---|
| `home` | dashboard, todos, post-its, memo dates, notifications |
| `stats` | the charts of the home page in tables, column charts and line charts: per year (revenue, per day, relative), per month, cumulated revenue, per client, hours (per year, progress, per client), dossiers, expenses per tag |
| `tasks` | reminders and scheduled actions (with their parameters), results, cron check |
| `timesheets` | `log` hours of a day, rates, settings, close / reopen, generate the invoice, pdf, stats |
| `expenses` | `add` from files (+ tag and price), tag, price, attach / detach, download, labels, exceptional expenses |
| `invoices` | list, guided `new` from a client, edit, pdf / peppol xml, manual upload, attachments, credit note, peppol validate / send, delete / restore |
| `dossiers` | active dossier, add / remove expenses, invoices, documents, close, recall, zip, summary / report / annual report pdf, import |
| `documents` | `upload` a file with title / tags, edit, download |
| `reports` | activity reports: write (markdown in the editor), attachments, post-its, messages, pdf |
| `gallery` | images of the public gallery |
| `cv` | show, edit (json), pdf, download requests |
| `finance` | portfolios with live quotes, symbols, search |
| `uploads` | every file: upload, download (zip), `search` inside files (full text index) |
| `sparql` | query the triplestore (table, json, csv, turtle…) |
| `prospects` | messages of the contact form |
| `clients` | billable clients, rates, contract status, documents |
| `mails` | send mails with files from paths, queue, retry |
| `templates` | `edit` a jinja template in `$EDITOR` with `preview` (mock data), add / replace / default |
| `admin` | company info (logo, signature…), menu, caches, scripts, sms, health, logs |
| `toolbox` | pdf split / rotate, rdf conversion, shacl, xpath |

Entities without a dedicated form (cv, an invoice before generation, a client, a task…) can be edited as
json in `$EDITOR` with `edit`: unknown fields are kept.

### Examples

```sh
# an expense from two files, tagged and priced
artcoded expenses add ticket.pdf receipt.jpg --subject "Train Brussels-Paris" --tag TRAVEL --price 120 --vat 0

# put the tagged expenses of the month in the active dossier and close it
artcoded dossiers add-expenses        # choose: 1,3-7 or all
artcoded dossiers close

# a document
artcoded documents upload ~/scan/statuts.pdf --tags legal,company

# the invoice of the month
artcoded timesheets close && artcoded timesheets invoice
artcoded invoices download --open

# edit the invoice template, preview it with mock data, save it
artcoded templates edit
artcoded templates mock <id> > ctx.json      # change it, then:
artcoded templates preview <id> --file draft.html --context ctx.json --open

# scripts
artcoded invoices list --json | jq '.content[].total'
```

## WhatsApp bot

The commands of the cli, from your "message yourself" chat on WhatsApp: `help`, `dashboard`, `invoices list`...
Missing arguments are asked in the chat (`.` for the default, `cancel` to stop). Send a file without text and the
bot asks what it is for (expense, document, payment proof...); or say it in the caption: `expense train ticket`,
`document Statuts 2026`, or any command taking files (`reports attach 12`). Downloads come back as files.

Try it in a terminal first, with a fake WhatsApp:

```sh
artcoded bot --console
help
/file ~/Downloads/ticket.pdf          # a file without text: the bot asks what it is for
/file ~/Downloads/ticket.pdf expense train ticket
/from 32471112233 help                # someone else (only the numbers of WHATSAPP_ALLOWED get an answer)
```

Then for real: the bot is a linked device of your own WhatsApp (like WhatsApp Web, no Business API).

```sh
ENABLE_WHATSAPP_BOT=true artcoded bot          # first time: a QR code, scan it in
                                               # WhatsApp > Settings > Linked devices > Link a device
ENABLE_WHATSAPP_BOT=true artcoded bot --phone 32470123456   # or a pairing code to type on the phone
artcoded bot status | logout
```

The bot answers you in your "message yourself" chat, and the numbers of `WHATSAPP_ALLOWED` in your chat with
them (they write to you; the answers come from your account). Everything else is ignored: other chats,
groups, the messages sent while the bot was down.

In docker the image runs `artcoded bot`; disabled, it just waits, so `docker exec` works:

```yaml
  cli:
    image: nbittich/artcoded-cli:latest
    restart: always
    environment:
      ENABLE_WHATSAPP_BOT: "true"
      WHATSAPP_ALLOWED: ""
    volumes:
      - ./data/cli:/data          # configuration, tokens, whatsapp session
```

```sh
docker compose exec cli artcoded login     # once: an offline token, renewed as long as it is used
docker compose logs -f cli                 # the QR code, the first time
```

| variable | |
|---|---|
| `ENABLE_WHATSAPP_BOT=true` | without it `artcoded bot` does not start (in a container: it waits) |
| `WHATSAPP_ALLOWED` | other numbers allowed to use the bot, in their own chat with it: `32471112233,32472...` |
| `WHATSAPP_SESSION` | the session file (default `~/.local/share/artcoded/whatsapp.db`, `/data/whatsapp.db` in docker) |
| `WHATSAPP_LOG_LEVEL` | `DEBUG`, `INFO`, `WARN` (default), `ERROR` |

## Configuration

`~/.config/artcoded-cli.yml` (`--config` or `ARTCODED_CONFIG` for another file). Every key can be
overridden with an environment variable `ARTCODED_<KEY>` (e.g. `ARTCODED_PASSWORD`).

```yaml
backend_url: "https://api.example.org"
frontend_url: "https://backoffice.example.org"
keycloak_url: "https://auth.example.org"
realm: "Artcoded"
client_id: "artcoded"
login_method: "password"
username: "nordine"
password: "…"                 # or password_command: "pass show artcoded"
redirect_port: "53682"        # browser login
sparql_endpoint: "https://api.example.org/sparql"
ca_file: "~/.local/share/mkcert/rootCA.pem"   # self-signed setup (or insecure: "true")
editor: "code --wait"         # default $VISUAL, $EDITOR, nano, vi
download_dir: "~/Downloads"   # default: the current directory
```

`artcoded config [show|edit|set <key> <value>]`.

## Releases

- **every tag `v*`** (`./release.sh`): tests, builds linux amd64 / arm64, publishes the GitHub release with
  the binaries and `checksums.txt`, pushes the docker image `:<tag>` and `:latest`; then the install
  section of this README is updated with the new version (a commit on `main`).
- **every push on `main`**: tests, builds, replaces the `edge` pre-release (`install.sh` with `edge`) and
  pushes the docker image `:edge`.

The docker images need the `DOCKER_USERNAME` / `DOCKER_PASSWORD` secrets of the repository (like the backend). Not called `latest`: on GitHub, `releases/latest` is the newest *stable* release.

The version (`artcoded version`) is the tag, or `edge-<commit>`.

## Development

```sh
go test ./...   # fake keycloak + backend: init, the three logins, menu, uploads, downloads, previews
```

The commands are in `mod_*.go`, one file per module; the routes are the ones of the backoffice
(`src/api/*.ts`).
